QtDateFormat

class QtDateFormat[source]

Bases: object

Convert Python strftime date formats to Qt formats.

Provides a clean separation between application configuration (strftime masks) and Qt presentation logic.

Methods

from_config() -> str

Return the Qt date format of the current application setting.

strftime_to_qt(strftime_mask) -> str

Convert an arbitrary strftime mask to Qt syntax.

format_python_date(python_date) -> str

Format a Python date using the configured Qt mask.

to_qdate(python_date) -> QDate

Convert a Python date or datetime object to QDate.

Examples

>>> QtDateFormat.strftime_to_qt('%d de %B de %Y')
'dd de MMMM de yyyy'

static from_config()[source]

Return the Qt date format of the application configuration.

The configured mask uses Python strftime syntax (e.g. "%d/%m/%Y"). This method returns the equivalent format string ready for Qt widgets.

Returns:
str

Format string suitable for QDateEdit.setDisplayFormat(), QDateTimeEdit.setDisplayFormat() or QDate.toString().

See also

strftime_to_qt

Low-level conversion function.

Notes

The mask is read from AppConfig.get_geral_date_mask() on every call.

static strftime_to_qt(strftime_mask)[source]

Convert a Python strftime mask to Qt format syntax.

Parameters:
strftime_maskstr

Date format using strftime directives, e.g. "%d/%m/%Y", "%Y-%m-%d" or "%d de %B de %Y".

Returns:
str

Equivalent format string understood by Qt.

Notes

Supported strftime to Qt mappings:

strftime

Qt

Description

%Y

yyyy

4-digit year

%y

yy

2-digit year

%m

MM

Month as zero-padded number (01-12)

%d

dd

Day as zero-padded number (01-31)

%B

MMMM

Full month name

%b

MMM

Abbreviated month name

%A

dddd

Full weekday name

%a

ddd

Abbreviated weekday name

Any other text, including other % directives, is kept unchanged and is not quoted. Qt reads unquoted letters such as d, M and y as format characters, so the literal “de” in "%d de %B de %Y" is shown by Qt as the day number followed by “e”. TODO(doc): should literal text be quoted ('de') in the Qt mask?

Examples

>>> QtDateFormat.strftime_to_qt("%d/%m/%Y")
'dd/MM/yyyy'

>>> QtDateFormat.strftime_to_qt("%Y-%m-%d")
'yyyy-MM-dd'

>>> QtDateFormat.strftime_to_qt("%d de %B de %Y")
'dd de MMMM de yyyy'

>>> QtDateFormat.strftime_to_qt("%a, %d %b %Y")
'ddd, dd MMM yyyy'
static format_python_date(python_date)[source]

Format a Python date object using the configured Qt mask.

Parameters:
python_datedate | datetime | None

Python date or datetime object to format.

Returns:
str

Formatted date string according to from_config(), or an empty string when python_date is None.

Notes

Only the date part is used; the time of a datetime is ignored.

static to_qdate(python_date)[source]

Convert a Python date or datetime object to QDate.

Parameters:
python_datedate | datetime | None

Python date or datetime object to convert.

Returns:
QDate

Corresponding Qt date, or the current date when python_date is None or falsy.

Examples

>>> from datetime import date
>>> qdate = QtDateFormat.to_qdate(date(2024, 1, 5))
>>> qdate.toString("yyyy-MM-dd")
'2024-01-05'
>>> QtDateFormat.to_qdate(None) == QDate.currentDate()
True
